title.narrative: Främjandet av grön tillväxt i textilsektorn genom kompetensutveckling (PROGRESS)
Promoting Green Growth in the RMG Sector Through Skills (PROGRESS)

description.narrative: *Detta bidrag klassificeras som ett typ A projekt enligt policymarkören för insatser som syftar till att stödja Team Sweden och den privata sektorn inom konfektions- och textilindustrin i Bangladesh.* Det föreslagna projektet “Promoting Green Growth in the RMG Sector Through Skills (PROGRESS)” har som mål att bidra till utvecklandet av en inkluderande, miljömässigt hållbar och konkurrenskraftig konfektionsindustri i Bangladesh som kan erbjuda produktiva, välbetalda och trygga arbetstillfällen med anständiga arbetsvillkor för framförallt kvinnor och att sektorn samtidigt anpassar sig till den globala marknadens förändrade krav på tekniska framsteg och på att fabrikerna lever upp till standarder relaterade till miljö, klimat och sociala förhållanden. Det föreslagna projektet kommer att ge teknisk utbildning till nuvarande arbetare inom textil och konfektionsindustrin med relativt låg kompetens. Tanken är att de nya tekniska kunskaperna som framförallt kvinnor och ungdomar erhåller genom projektet kommer att öka deras chanser att bibehålla sin anställning när fabrikerna i allt större utsträckning automatiseras, och att vissa färdigheter även kan överföras till andra sektorer om arbetarna ändå skulle förlora sin anställning i textilsektorn. Utbildningen som ges till de fabriksanställda och fabrikernas ledningar kommer även att innehålla aspekter för att öka deras medvetenhet om vikten av gender och miljö- och klimataspekter.

*This contribution is tagged as a type A project in terms of the policy marker for contributing to Team Sweden/Private Sector in the ready-made garment/textile sectors in Bangladesh.* The project “Promoting Green Growth in the RMG Sector Through Skills (PROGRESS)” aims to contribute to the development of an inclusive, environmentally responsible, and competitive RMG sector in Bangladesh that can offer productive, well paid, secured, and decent job opportunities to workers, mostly women, and at the same time, adapt to the evolving needs of the global market in terms of technological advancement and ESG standards. The proposed project aims to provide technical training to currently employed workers in the RMG sector with relatively low skill-levels, primarily women and youth. The idea is that the technical obtained through the project will enhance the chances of these women retaining employment despite automation, and that some skills obtained may also be transferable to other sectors if they lose their employment in the RMG sector. Furthermore, gender and environment and climate change aspects will be included in the training provided to factory employees and management.

The project envisions contributing to the development of an inclusive, environmentally responsible, and competitive RMG sector in Bangladesh that can offer productive, well paid, secured, and decent job opportunities to workers, mostly women, and at the same time, adapt to the evolving needs of the global market in terms of technological advancement and environmental and social standards. By supporting RMG factories and implementing sustainable skills training system the project aligns its objectives with Swedens aim of creating greater opportunities for productive employment with decent working conditions for RMG workers. The project has two goals envisioned to be achieved during the four years of the project period:
Project Goal 1: RMG workers (including 60% women) have better retention rates and increased income due to improved technical skills and productivity,
Project Goal 2: Tier-2 and Tier-3 RMG factories have improved productivity and, environmental and social compliance and are offering decent employment to their workers.
The goals will be achieved through a variety of activities, including:
- the provision of technical support to tier-2 and tier-3 factories for technical skills development of RMG workers,
- technical support to tier-2 and tier-3 factories to improve productivity, and environmental and social standards, as well as
- the development of capacity of local technical consultancy providers for service delivery related to skills which enhance the compliance of RMG factories with environmental and social standards and increase these factories productivity.
These objectives are assessed to correspond to the development results that Sida is expecting from this project.

Summary of Achieved Results 2024
Promoting Green Growth in the RMG Sector Through Skills (PROGRESS) project implemented by Swisscontact Bangladesh has delivered a range of impactful results during 2024, contributing to inclusive and green transformation in the Ready-Made Garment (RMG) sector in Bangladesh. The programme has effectively applied results-based management and adapted dynamically to evolving needs. Below is a summary of some of the most important expected and unexpected results achieved, with a focus on real changes experienced by the target groups and stakeholders.
Expected Results Achieved
The project has significantly improved the skills and productivity of RMG workers. In 2024, over 6,800 workers, including 4,783 women, were trained through Industry-Based Training (IBT), leading to a 29% increase in hourly productivity. Workers who were previously underperforming gained the ability to meet production targets more efficiently, resulting in enhanced job security and factory performance.
In parallel, the Womens Leadership Training Programme (WLTP) equipped 14 female workers with the technical and soft skills necessary to move into supervisory rolessomething they were not able to do previously. All of them were promoted to supervisory positions during the reporting year, and some received up to a 47% salary increase. This outcome has changed both workplace dynamics and individual career trajectories for these women.
The project also delivered strong results in the area of environmental and social compliance. Nine factories developed Climate Action Roadmaps and initiated steps toward carbon accounting and energy efficiency. These efforts were supported by training programmes on sustainability reporting and green skills. Over 950 workersprimarily womenwere trained on energy and water conservation, safe chemical handling, and waste reduction. Workers reported behaviour changes such as turning off machines and reducing water usesmall actions that collectively contribute to significant environmental gains.
Factory co-investment was another key outcome. Factories invested a total of SEK 1.27 million into productivity and ESG initiatives supported by the project. For example, Fakhruddin Textile Mills Ltd. realized a return on investment of SEK 170,000 within a year by applying the Zero-Defect Operator (ZDO) model. This shows that factories are no longer passive recipients but are becoming active investors in sustainable business practices.
Additionally, the project recorded early signs of positive wage impacts. Over 3,300 workersmore than 70% of them womenreceived wage increments during the reporting period, totaling SEK 2.8 million. While national wage adjustments and business performance played a role, improved worker efficiency, influenced by project interventions, contributed meaningfully to these outcomes.
Unexpected Results Observed
Beyond the anticipated outcomes, PROGRESS produced several unexpected yet highly significant results.
First, the Womens Leadership Training Programme (WLTP) sparked a notable cultural shift in factories. While the programme focused on technical skills, its broader influence led to increased acceptance of female supervisors among peers and management. This was especially notable in factories where women had never before held leadership roles. The initiative helped redefine perceptions of womens capabilities in the workplace and opened the door to long-term gender norm shifts in the sector.
Second, there was unsolicited demand from factories to continue and even expand sustainability-focused training. For example, Belamy Textiles Ltd. voluntarily requested additional green skills training and integrated it into their internal training schedule. This kind of initiative indicates that some factories are beginning to internalize environmental responsibility as part of their business modelan unanticipated yet welcome result.
Another unexpected outcome was the strategic interest from international brands in applying the PROGRESS model upstream in the RMG supply chain. Brands have expressed a strong interest in seeing similar interventions in sectors such as packaging, accessories, and textiles. This signals that the projects influence is extending beyond direct beneficiaries and into broader supply chain practices.
Finally, the project noted early wage effects linked to performance. Although salary increases were not a primary project objective at this stage, trained workersespecially womendemonstrated strong productivity and were rewarded accordingly. This has started to influence factory HR practices, where performance-based pay is gaining more traction.
Conclusion
The Embassy concludes that the PROGRESS project is demonstrating real and tangible changes in the RMG sector, particularly among factory workers, management, and service providers. Workers are acquiring market-relevant skills, women are moving into leadership roles, factories are investing in sustainability, and attitudes toward gender and green practices are evolving. The projects approachcombining skills development, ESG compliance, gender inclusion, and private sector engagementis yielding both expected and unforeseen benefits, making a measurable difference in the sector. This success provides a strong foundation for the next phase of implementation, including deeper factory-level engagement, expansion into new supply chain segments, and stronger partnerships with brands and financial institutions.
